target_customer: Pharmacies in Canada (Alberta first) that want reformulated versions of common drugs for specific patient groups
problem: About half of patients do not take medications as prescribed, often due to unpleasant formats; pharmacies lack a supply of reformulated products.
business_model: B2B marketplace supplying compounded reformulated drugs from compounders to pharmacies

founders.name: Morenike Eniola Olaosebikan
founders.background_notes: Licensed clinical pharmacist and pharmacy proprietor, clinical academic colleague at the Faculty of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, University of Alberta (YC page); founded Kemet in 2016 per Taproot Edmonton.

technical_complexity.rationale: A supply platform on top of provincially regulated compounding; the difficulty is regulatory and pharmaceutical, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Compounding rules limit who can supply, but any compounder could sell reformulations directly.

market_need_then: In Sept 2022 KemNet supplied three compounders and 30 Alberta pharmacies (Taproot Edmonton). Pharmacies typically compound only when no Health Canada approved product exists, which constrains demand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful launch post title 'Because Not All Pills Should Be Swallowed!' with emojis.

branding.brand_signature: Launch line: Because Not All Pills Should Be Swallowed

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence about the brand itself; name resembles the founder's Kemet company, unconfirmed.

outcome_analysis: KemNet joined YC in Summer 2022 with an Alberta pharmacy supply platform for reformulated drugs and had 30 pharmacies and three compounders at that time. No funding round, exit or shutdown is reported publicly, and a third party estimate puts revenue at about 880,000 dollars in 2025. The story is unclear: regulatory limits on compounding may cap growth but there is no evidence of failure.
notes: Website kemnet.ca returned 503, so it could not be fetched.
